subject: Bridgetech TIA: caching/proxying residency and subprocessor access
messages:
From: Sara Wilson <sara.wilson@bridgetech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy@bridgetech.com
Date: 2027-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: TIA scoping: caching, proxying, onshore fallback

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our privacy team is preparing the TIA checklist for legal review and we had a couple of technical clarifications before we proceed:

1) Caching: Bridgetech needs to confirm that any prefix/KV caches used by Redwood for inference are not persisted or replicated to the US when the production workload is EU-only. Can you confirm if prefix caches (short-term KV) are stored only in-region or if they flow to any cross-border analytics/export services?

2) Proxying / onshore fallback: You mentioned an onshore cache fallback for latency – will requests that hit the onshore fallback ever route user data out of the EU for model execution, or is the fallback limited to EU-based model variants? We need the operational behaviour documented for the TIA.

3) Subprocessor access: which subprocessors might touch the cached artifacts (logs, traces, cache manifests)? We need a short list and a pointer to attestation timelines.

Could you attach a simple network diagram showing ingress/egress zones and an evidence checklist we can attach to the TIA?

Appreciate the quick turn — we’re hoping to get the packet to legal by end of week.

Best,
Sara
Privacy Counsel, Bridgetech

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Wilson <sara.wilson@bridgetech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TIA scoping: caching, proxying, onshore fallback

Hi Sara —

Thanks — quick answers up front, then we’ll follow with a short evidence packet + diagram.

• Caching: Runtime prefix/KV caches are regional by default. For an EU-only deployment we pin cache residency to the EU region and do not replicate KV contents to US analytics. Non-persistent telemetry (aggregated metrics) may cross regions for platform health, but not raw cache contents.

• Onshore fallback: Fallback is configurable per-customer. For Bridgetech we can configure the policy so that fallbacks only use EU model variants and EU-hosted inference pools. If you want the onshore fallback disabled entirely we can do that too.

• Subprocessors: Short list is below — I’ll ask Naomi to attach the latest attestation ETA and network diagram.
  - Cloud provider infra (regional edge): AWS eu-west-1 (subprocessor: cloud-edge-provider)
  - Monitoring/metrics (aggregated telemetry): thirdparty-metrics-inc
  - Managed key store (optional): redwood-kms-partner (if customer enables external KMS)

I’m attaching a draft checklist (bridgetech_tia_checklist.xlsx) and looping Naomi for legal/infra confirmation. Propose a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the TIA packet before you share with legal.

Best,
Kimberly
Lead, Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: bridgetech_tia_checklist.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: TIA scoping: caching, proxying, onshore fallback (Bridgetech)

Folks — forwarding Bridgetech’s questions (below). They specifically want:

- Confirmation that prefix/KV caches for EU-only customers stay in-region (no replication to US)
- Explicit operational description for the onshore fallback and whether any execution or caching will cross borders when fallback triggers
- Which subprocessors might touch cache artifacts and when we can provide attestation evidence

Rishi — can infra confirm the following by EOD?
  1) For EU-only model pools, are any cache manifests, persisted shards, or cold-start artifacts ever uploaded to global S3 buckets or US telemetry pipelines? We should list exact artifact types and flow.
  2) Does the onshore fallback ever execute on non-EU GPUs or route tokens outside region if EU capacity is exhausted? If yes, what are the exact conditions and can we provide a “strict-EU” toggle for Bridgetech?

Naomi — can legal confirm whether our standard UK Addendum / IDTA language covers the fallback behaviour, or if we should propose an explicit clause in the TIA to prevent cross-border fallback for this account?

I’m attaching the customer-facing checklist we plan to send.

—Kim

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sara Wilson <sara.wilson@bridgetech.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-24T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: TIA scoping: caching, proxying, onshore fallback

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the clear list — apologies for the slight delay while we pulled infra/ops confirmation together. Please find the consolidated responses and attached diagram. Short summary below and next steps at the end.

1) Prefix/KV cache residency
   - Technical behaviour: prefix/KV caches used by our inference runtime are ephemeral and resident in the serving region. For an EU-only deployment (we’ll reflect this in your TIA), cache shards and KV entries are created on regional ephemeral storage and will not be replicated to US storage or global buckets.
   - Exceptions: aggregated, de-identified platform metrics and sampling telemetry (e.g., token throughput, error rates) may be transmitted to our metrics provider for health and SLO tracking; those streams contain no raw prompt/response content.

2) Onshore fallback behaviour
   - By default Redwood can be configured either to (A) restrict fallbacks to EU-hosted model variants only, or (B) allow cross-region fallback when EU capacity is exhausted. For Bridgetech we recommend and can enforce policy (A) — we will document a strict-EU toggle in the TIA so fallback cannot route execution to non-EU GPUs.

3) Subprocessors touching cache artifacts
   - Short list (operational role):
     • cloud-edge-provider (regional infra) — may host ephemeral cache storage
     • thirdparty-metrics-inc — receives aggregated telemetry only (no raw cache contents)
     • redwood-kms-partner — only relevant if customer enables external key management
   - Attestation timeline: cloud-edge-provider and thirdparty-metrics-inc attestation packages available within 7 business days; full subprocessor CSV and signed statements in 14 business days.

Attachments included: network-diagram.pdf (shows EU ingress/egress, cache residency, fallback workflow), bridgetech_tia_checklist.xlsx (updated with the strict-EU toggle and subprocessor ETA).

Next steps:
• Please confirm you want the strict-EU fallback enforced (we will add a line to the TIA and update the DPA/UK Addendum language).
• If yes, we’ll provide the subprocessor attestation by 2027-04-07 and a final TIA packet for legal to review.

If you’d like a short call to walk the diagram I’m available tomorrow morning EU hours.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
